title: node:ffi
lede: Node's experimental node:ffi module (v26.1.0+) — call C functions from shared libraries, or from the process itself, with plain-object signatures, and peek/poke native memory through bigint pointers. Because this is an AOT compiler, a signature written at the call site is resolved at compile time and lowered to a direct, correctly-typed C-ABI call through the dlsym'd pointer — no libffi, no generic marshalling tier, so every call takes what Node documents as the fast path. 64-bit integers and pointers travel as bigint, strings pass as NUL-terminated UTF-8, and Buffers/typed arrays/ArrayBuffers pass their backing data pointer, exactly as in Node. dlopen(null) opens the current process image, so libc is callable with zero setup. The raw-memory helper set (getInt8…setFloat64, toString/toBuffer/toArrayBuffer with zero-copy views, exportString/exportBuffer, getRawPointer) is in. registerCallback hands a closure to C as a real function pointer — statically-emitted trampoline families per signature, so a KlainMainLang comparator can drive libc's qsort. POSIX only for now.

entries.name: ffi.dlopen(path, definitions?)
entries.signature: dlopen(path: string | null, definitions?: Record<string, { arguments?: string[], return?: string }>): { lib: DynamicLibrary, functions: Record<string, Function> }
entries.description: Loads a shared library (or the current process image for null) and resolves every function in definitions in one step. The definitions map must be an object literal — each signature is resolved at compile time and the call lowers to a direct C-ABI call. The path may be any runtime string. Failures throw an Error carrying dlerror().

returns.desc: The library handle plus one callable per definition.

entries.name: new DynamicLibrary(path) / lib.close() / ffi.dlclose(lib)
entries.signature: new DynamicLibrary(path: string | null); close(): void; dlclose(lib: DynamicLibrary): void
entries.description: Opens a library without resolving anything yet; lib.path reads the path back. close() releases the handle and is idempotent, as in Node. `using` declarations and [Symbol.dispose]() are not supported yet — explicit close() is the disposal path.

entries.name: lib.getFunction(name, signature) / lib.getFunctions(definitions)
entries.signature: getFunction(name: string, signature: { arguments?: string[], return?: string }): Function; getFunctions(definitions: object): Record<string, Function>
entries.description: Binds one native symbol (or a map of them) to a directly-callable function. The signature must be a compile-time object literal; type names accept every Node alias spelling (i32, ptr, str, double, …) and the ffi.types constants. The bound function's .pointer property is its raw address as a bigint. Re-resolving the same symbol with a different signature is not diagnosed (Node throws).

returns.desc: A callable lowered to a direct C-ABI call.

entries.name: lib.getSymbol(name) / ffi.dlsym(lib, name)
entries.signature: getSymbol(name: string): bigint; dlsym(lib: DynamicLibrary, name: string): bigint
entries.description: Resolves a symbol to its raw address as a bigint. A missing symbol throws a catchable Error carrying dlerror().

entries.name: Typed calls + marshalling
entries.description: Arguments convert per the declared type: numbers for ints up to 32 bits and floats, bigint for int64/uint64 and pointers (plain numbers are also accepted for 64-bit parameters — looser than Node, which requires bigint), strings pass NUL-terminated UTF-8, and Buffer/typed-array/ArrayBuffer arguments pass their backing data pointer. Returns widen back the same way; pointer returns are bigint addresses and string returns copy the C string (null → null). function-typed values pass as raw bigint addresses; creating one from a closure needs registerCallback (not shipped).

entries.name: lib.functions / lib.symbols / lib.getFunctions() / lib.getSymbols()
entries.signature: functions: Record<string, Function>; symbols: Record<string, bigint>; getFunctions(): Record<string, Function>; getSymbols(): Record<string, bigint>
entries.description: Node's accumulators of everything previously resolved through the library: functions holds the callable typed wrappers (dlopen definitions plus getFunction registrations), symbols every resolved address as a bigint, in resolution order. Here the record is compile-time — names registered through literal getFunction/getSymbol calls and definitions maps on that library value; a runtime-computed name is resolved but not recorded. Addresses are re-dlsym'd at the read point, so the returned object is an ordinary object (Object.keys, destructuring, and calls all work).

returns.desc: Callable wrappers or bigint addresses, keyed by name.

entries.name: lib.registerCallback / unregisterCallback / refCallback / unrefCallback
entries.signature: registerCallback(signature: { arguments?: string[], return?: string }, callback: Function): bigint; unregisterCallback(pointer: bigint): void; refCallback(pointer: bigint): void; unrefCallback(pointer: bigint): void
entries.description: Hands a closure to C as a raw function pointer: the returned bigint is a real C-callable address whose invocations marshal the C arguments into your callback's declared types and the return back out (64-bit and pointer parameters must be declared bigint, string as string). Implemented as statically-emitted per-signature trampoline families over a registration table — no runtime code generation — which caps concurrently-live callbacks at 16 per signature shape (exceeding it throws; unregistered slots recycle). refCallback/unrefCallback are validated no-ops (registered callbacks are always strongly referenced), and close() does not invalidate callbacks — unregister explicitly.

entries.name: ffi.getInt8…getFloat64 / ffi.setInt8…setFloat64
entries.signature: getInt32(pointer: bigint, offset?: number): number; setInt32(pointer: bigint, offset: number, value: number): void; getInt64(...): bigint; setInt64(..., value: bigint): void
entries.description: Read and write native memory at a bigint address plus a byte offset. All ten widths in both directions: 8/16/32-bit values are numbers, 64-bit values are bigint (exact — values above 2^53 round-trip), float32 narrows through double. Getter offsets are optional (default 0); setter offsets are required, matching Node. No bounds checking — the module's documented unsafe posture.

returns.desc: The read value; setters return nothing.

entries.name: ffi.toString / toBuffer / toArrayBuffer / getRawPointer
entries.signature: toString(pointer: bigint): string | null; toBuffer(pointer: bigint, length: number, copy?: boolean): Buffer; toArrayBuffer(pointer: bigint, length: number, copy?: boolean): ArrayBuffer; getRawPointer(src: Buffer | ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView): bigint
entries.description: Bring native memory into JS values. toString reads a NUL-terminated UTF-8 C string (null for 0n). toBuffer/toArrayBuffer take length bytes — copied by default, or as a zero-copy view with copy: false (the caller keeps the memory valid, Node's contract). getRawPointer goes the other way: the backing data pointer of a Buffer/ArrayBuffer/view as a bigint address.
entries.snippet:
const s = ffi.toString(ptr);
const view = ffi.toBuffer(ptr, 16, false); // zero-copy

entries.name: ffi.exportString / exportBuffer / exportArrayBuffer / exportArrayBufferView
entries.signature: exportString(str: string, pointer: bigint, length: number, encoding?: 'utf8'): void; exportBuffer(src: Buffer, pointer: bigint, length: number): void; exportArrayBuffer(src: ArrayBuffer, pointer: bigint, length: number): void; exportArrayBufferView(src: ArrayBufferView, pointer: bigint, length: number): void
entries.description: Copy JS data into caller-provided native memory. exportString writes the UTF-8 bytes NUL-terminated, truncating to the capacity; only the 'utf8' encoding is supported (this compiler's strings are UTF-8-native). The byte-export forms copy the source's bytes and throw a RangeError when length is smaller than the source's byteLength, as in Node.

entries.name: ffi.suffix / ffi.types
entries.description: suffix is the host's shared-library filename suffix ('dylib' on macOS, 'so' on Linux, 'dll' on Windows), a compile-time constant. ffi.types holds the type-name string constants (ffi.types.INT_32 === 'int32', …) usable anywhere a type name goes in a signature.
